questions.subject: English Language
questions.text:
Across many small towns and rural communities, entrepreneurship has become one of the most reliable paths out of poverty, especially where formal employment is scarce. A young tailor who once served only her immediate neighbours can, with a smartphone and a modest data plan, now showcase her designs to customers hundreds of kilometres away. Microfinance institutions and cooperative societies have also made small loans more accessible, allowing traders and artisans to expand their businesses without depending on relatives or moneylenders. Even so, many entrepreneurs still struggle with unreliable electricity, poor road networks, and limited access to affordable credit, all of which raise the cost of doing business. Governments and development agencies increasingly recognise that supporting small and medium enterprises is not merely a charitable gesture but a sound strategy for building resilient, self-sustaining local economies.

According to the passage, what has enabled a small-town tailor to reach distant customers?
options: A large factory built with foreign investment
A partnership with a multinational retailer
A smartphone and a modest data plan
questions.explanation: The passage states that with 'a smartphone and a modest data plan', the tailor can showcase her designs to customers far away.

Able to recover from difficulties and remain strong

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: 'Neither the manager nor the staff ___ aware of the change.'
questions.explanation: With 'neither...nor', the verb agrees with the subject nearer to it ('the staff' is closer, but in strict traditional grammar with a singular first noun and this construction pattern, 'was' agrees with the nearer singular sense expected here); standard practice: the verb agrees with the nearest subject, 'staff' functioning as a collective singular unit in this context, giving 'was'.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word: 'Her ARDUOUS journey to the village took three days.'
questions.explanation: 'Arduous' means involving strenuous effort or difficulty, making 'difficult and tiring' the closest synonym.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the underlined word: 'The new regulations were met with UNANIMOUS approval.'
questions.explanation: 'Unanimous' means everyone in agreement; its opposite is 'divided', meaning split in opinion.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: 'Accommodate' is correctly spelt with double 'c' and double 'm'; the other options misspell the word.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: 'If I ___ you, I would apologise immediately.'
questions.explanation: This is a second conditional expressing a hypothetical situation, requiring the subjunctive 'were' regardless of subject.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the correct preposition to complete the sentence: 'The book is quite similar ___ the one I read last year.'
questions.explanation: 'Similar to' is the standard and correct preposition pairing in English usage.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Identify the part of speech of the underlined word: 'The SUDDENLY loud noise startled everyone.'
questions.explanation: 'Suddenly' modifies the adjective 'loud', describing the manner of the noise becoming loud, making it an adverb.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option that is the correct plural form of 'crisis'.
questions.explanation: 'Crisis', derived from Greek, forms its plural irregularly as 'crises'.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the idiom: 'The manager decided to TURN A BLIND EYE to the minor infraction.'
questions.explanation: 'Turn a blind eye' is an idiom meaning to deliberately ignore or pretend not to notice something.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option that correctly completes the sentence: 'Mathematics ___ a compulsory subject in secondary school.'
questions.explanation: Although 'mathematics' ends in 's', it is treated as a singular subject when referring to the academic discipline, requiring 'is'.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the word that best completes the sentence: 'The ___ evidence convinced the jury of his guilt.'
questions.explanation: 'Conclusive' is the adjective form needed to describe the evidence as decisive and final.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence.
options: Please bring the following, a pen a notebook and a calculator.
Please bring the following: a pen, a notebook, and a calculator.
Please bring the following a pen, a notebook, and a calculator.
Please bring the following; a pen, a notebook, and a calculator.
questions.explanation: A colon correctly introduces the list following the complete independent clause 'Please bring the following.'

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: 'The information he provided ___ inaccurate.'
questions.explanation: 'Information' is an uncountable noun that takes a singular verb, so 'was inaccurate' is correct.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Identify the figure of speech used: 'The wind whispered through the trees.'
questions.explanation: Giving the wind the human ability to 'whisper' attributes a human action to a non-human thing, making this personification.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word: 'The company's growth has been remarkably RAPID.'
questions.explanation: 'Rapid' means happening at a fast pace, making 'very fast' the closest synonym.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the correct form of the verb: 'Each of the students ___ expected to submit an assignment.'
questions.explanation: 'Each' is grammatically singular, so it takes the singular verb 'is', regardless of the plural noun that follows.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: 'This is the town ___ history dates back centuries.'
questions.explanation: 'Whose' is the possessive relative pronoun correctly used to link 'the town' to 'its history.'

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the word opposite in meaning to the underlined word: 'The results of the experiment were CONCLUSIVE.'
questions.explanation: 'Conclusive' means decisive or definite; its direct opposite is 'inconclusive', meaning not leading to a firm conclusion.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the correct option to complete the sentence: 'He is not only intelligent ___ also hardworking.'
questions.explanation: The correlative pairing 'not only...but also' is the standard grammatical construction linking two related qualities.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Identify the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: 'Necessary' is correctly spelt with one 'c' and double 's'; the other options are misspellings.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: 'It was they who ___ blamed for the delay.'
questions.explanation: The subject 'they' requires the plural past tense verb 'were' for grammatical agreement.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word: 'The professor's argument was remarkably COGENT.'
questions.explanation: 'Cogent' means clear, logical, and convincing, especially of an argument.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the correct option: 'This decision affects both you and ___.'
questions.explanation: After the conjunction 'and' within a prepositional object position, the objective case pronoun 'me' is correct.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option that correctly completes the sentence: 'The majority of the residents ___ opposed to the new tax.'
questions.explanation: 'The majority of' followed by a plural noun ('residents') takes a plural verb.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option that best expresses the meaning of the sentence: 'She decided to bite the bullet and accept the challenging assignment.'
options: She chose to face a difficult situation bravely
She literally bit down on a bullet
She refused to accept the assignment
questions.explanation: 'Bite the bullet' is an idiom meaning to face a difficult or unpleasant situation with courage.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the word that is nearest in meaning to the underlined word: 'The old building was in a state of complete DECREPITUDE.'
options: Being worn out and in poor condition
questions.explanation: 'Decrepitude' refers to a state of being worn out or in poor condition due to age or neglect.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Everybody have to bring his own textbook.
Everybody has to bring they own textbook.
Everybody have to bring their own textbook.
Everybody has to bring his or her own textbook.
questions.explanation: 'Everybody' is grammatically singular, so it takes the singular verb 'has' and a singular possessive form in formal usage.
